mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_STAFF + i from Staff{i+1}, so Staff01.bmd is staff index 0, which openmu's 0.75 Weapons.cs names the Skull Staff. mu.db agrees: group 5 index 0, Item/Staff01.bmd.
why_this_one: Pasi's, and the last four lines he sells. The mage stocks all four staves - the Skull at +0, the Angelic at +2, the Serpent and the Thunder at +3 - and none was built, so four of his nineteen lines were dropped by Realm.Shelf. With these he sells all nineteen. See shared/Market.Mage.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: WeaponInitializerBase.CreateWeapon(group, number, slot, skillNumber, width, height, dropsFromMonsters, name, dropLevel, minimumDamage, maximumDamage, attackSpeed, durability, magicPower, levelRequirement, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, energyRequirement, vitalityRequirement, wizardClass, knightClass, elfClass).
stats.width_note: Width does not mean two-handed here and cannot: OpenMU's test is `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` and Bows is 4, so nothing in group 5 is ever caught by it. Two-handedness comes from MuWeapons.cs alone, which is the client's own table, and within this group of four it disagrees three times to one.
stats.magic_power_note: magic_power is the column no weapon built here has carried before. Every sword, axe and bow in the project passes 0 for it and the four staves pass 6, 20, 34 and 46 - it is the wizard's damage, where a blade's is the min and max above. Recorded and unread: shared/Combat.cs rolls physical damage off the weapon row and has no spell in it yet.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 1, 0, 0 - the Dark Wizard alone, on all four.

stance_from:
MuWeapons.cs: WeaponStance.Sword, TwoHanded: false. The stance enum says why in its own comments - Sword is 'a one-handed sword, mace, or a one-handed staff' and Scythe is 'a scythe, or any two-handed staff or polearm' - so a staff takes the stance its handedness gives it and there is no staff stance. Actions 4 and 17.

The odd one of the four: the only one-handed staff in the group and therefore the only one that leaves the shield hand free.
sheet_from: Data/Item/wand02.OZJ (64x64), from MuMain, and the only sheet the model names - 150 triangles on one page. The .bmd names wand02.jpg. The staff models wear sheets called wand: MU numbered the art for the wands and the staves share it, which is the file naming and not a mismatch.
sheet_note: wand02 is a horned gold skull on a fluted gold shaft, drawn large with two smaller views beside it. Mean (131, 109, 74) at chroma 58 - a warm gold, and the skull is gold too rather than bone: it is cast metal in the shape of a skull, which is what the highlights along the brow say.
material_note:
Two islands and one answer. Island 1 is 96 triangles, the horned skull, and island 0 is 54, the fluted shaft; sampled per triangle at its own UV centre - the reading the polearms taught - they mean (130, 96, 45) and (117, 89, 48) at chroma 85 and 69. That is gold on both, so both take brass.

brass rather than plate_steel because of what the thing is: a skull and a fluted pole are poured in a mould, not beaten to fit a chest. That is the whole distinction those two files draw, and it is the reading the Brass set's ornaments got. The skull is gold and not bone - the highlights run along the brow the way they run on metal, and bone.json's own dead-white is nowhere on this sheet.
material_overrides_note: 2026-09-21, from the studio sheet: at brass's 0.45 the crossbar and the horns mirrored dusk's low sun into glowing bars with bloom (225-315 deg). Brass at 0.6 spreads the highlight, as for the Serpent Sword's grip and the Dragon Lance.
